case.summary: NARA letter to DHS CIO regarding potential loss of Signal/text messages by IG Joseph Cuffari and others.

evidence.statement: NARA has been made aware of the potential loss of electronic messages, including text messages and Signal messages, within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
evidence.quote: potential loss of electronic messages, including text messages and Signal messages, within the Department of Homeland Security

evidence.statement: DHS Inspector General Joseph Cuffari testified he used Signal only for a single phone call, for which no record was maintained.
evidence.quote: he stated that he was one of a small number of Department officials who used Signal at the direction of the Department following a security breach in late 2020 and early 2021.

evidence.statement: Mr. Cuffari stated he deleted text messages from his government phone because he did not consider them to be federal records.
evidence.quote: Mr. Cuffari also stated in his June 6, 2023, testimony that he deleted text messages from his government phone because he did not consider them to be federal records.

evidence.statement: It is Mr. Cuffari's practice to routinely delete text messages from his government phone.
evidence.quote: He further stated it is his practice to routinely delete text messages from his government phone.

evidence.statement: NARA requests that DHS confirm that all electronic messages sent or received by DHS officials using Signal have been managed in accordance with the Federal Records Act.
evidence.quote: NARA requests that DHS look into this matter and confirm that all electronic messages sent or received by DHS officials using Signal have been managed in accordance with the Federal Records Act.

evidence.statement: NARA requests that DHS provide NARA with the required report documenting IG Cuffari's practices with respect to the management of electronic messages.
evidence.quote: In accordance with 36 CFR 1230.16(b), NARA requests that DHS provide NARA with the required report documenting IG Cuffari's practices with respect to the management of electronic messages

entities.name: Kenneth T. Cuccinelli
entities.role: Former Senior Official Performing the Duties of the Deputy Secretary for DHS

entities.name: Laurence Brewer
entities.role: Chief Records Officer for the U.S. Government

uncertainty_notes: The letter states that the capture and preservation of messages beyond senior officials Chad F. Wolf and Kenneth T. Cuccinelli is unknown.
It is unclear if other DHS officials used Signal besides Joseph Cuffari, Chad F. Wolf, and Kenneth T. Cuccinelli.

case.summary: NARA acknowledges receipt of a DOJ report regarding the loss of 46 Microsoft OneDrive accounts containing Capstone user records, FOIA requests, and other federal records. The incident occurred during synchronization between Azure Active Directory and M365 SharePoint. NARA states that reporting requirements under 36 CFR 1230.14(a) have been met and considers the matter closed after DOJ implemented additional quality assurance checks and weekly reconciliation reporting.

evidence.statement: the loss of 46 Microsoft OneDrive accounts
evidence.quote: report on the loss of 46 Microsoft OneDrive accounts

evidence.statement: accounts containing Capstone user records were lost
evidence.quote: the 46 accounts containing Capstone user records

evidence.statement: records related to Freedom of Information Act requests were lost
evidence.quote: records related to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests

evidence.statement: other unidentifiable federal records were lost
evidence.quote: and other unidentifiable federal records were lost

evidence.statement: incident occurred during synchronization between Azure Active Directory and the M365 SharePoint
evidence.quote: during synchronization between Azure Active Directory and the M365 SharePoint

evidence.statement: DOJ updated process for closing accounts with additional quality assurance checks
evidence.quote: the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)/Service Delivery Staff (SDS) updated the process for closing accounts

entities.name: Office of the Chief Information Officer

uncertainty_notes: The specific date of the account loss incident is not explicitly stated in the provided text.
The exact number of records lost beyond the count of accounts (46) is not specified.

case.summary: NARA letter to DoD OIG regarding unauthorized disposal of departed employee email accounts on SIPRNET/JWICS.

evidence.statement: DODOIG has reported that email accounts of departed employees between 2022 and 2024 were disposed of without authorization.
evidence.quote: DODOIG has reported that email accounts of departed employees between 2022 and 2024 were disposed of without authorization

evidence.statement: Lost records covered by GRS 6.1 items 010, 011, and 012.
evidence.quote: the lost email records were covered by the General Records Schedule (GRS) 6.1 items 010, 011, and 012.

evidence.statement: Records destroyed due to a gap in implementation of protocols.
evidence.quote: the records were destroyed because of a "gap in the implementation of protocols" for email retention.

evidence.statement: DODOIG could not determine volume or recover lost records.
evidence.quote: DODOIG could not determine the volume of lost records or recover them.

evidence.statement: Gap identified and fixed by new rules and backup server.
evidence.quote: the gap in protocols that permitted the loss of records had been identified and fixed by implementing new system retention rules and creating a backup retention server.

evidence.statement: NARA requests details on protocol gap and scope.
evidence.quote: Please provide more details regarding the "gap in the implementation of protocols." What does this mean, and how did this gap influence the loss of email records?

entities.name: Department of Defense Office of Inspector General

uncertainty_notes: The exact volume of lost records is unknown per agency report.
Recovery of lost records is not possible per agency report.
Scope beyond DODOIG is under investigation by NARA.
Specific changes made after loss are requested but not yet provided.

case.summary: NARA closed a case regarding unauthorized destruction of federal records at a former U.S. Attorney's home, noting conflicting information about flood damage versus electronic record recovery.

evidence.statement: NARA has received the Department of Justice's report of the unauthorized destruction of federal records.
evidence.quote: The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) has received the Department of Justice's report of the unauthorized destruction of federal records

evidence.statement: Records were located in a former United States Attorney's home basement and destroyed in a flood.
evidence.quote: According to DOJ's report, the records were in a former United States Attorney's home basement. These records, according to information provided to DOJ, were then destroyed in a flood

evidence.statement: DOJ-OIG report found the former U.S. Attorney used personal cellphone text message feature and personal e-mail to conduct government business.
evidence.quote: Specifically, this former U.S. Attorney was found to have used a personal cellphone text message feature and personal e-mail to conduct government business.

evidence.statement: DOJ stated it is unable to determine which records were lost in the flood or if they were recordkeeping copies.
evidence.quote: DOJ further shared that it is unable to determine which records were lost in the flood at the former U.S. Attorney's house

evidence.statement: DOJ reported attempts to retrieve records through written requests to the former U.S. Attorney's representative were unsuccessful.
evidence.quote: DOJ reported to NARA that it has attempted to retrieve the records on numerous occasions through written requests submitted to this former U.S. Attorney's representative

evidence.statement: NARA considers this matter closed despite DOJ being unable to supply all information listed in 36 CFR §1230.14.
evidence.quote: Based on the information received, NARA considers this matter closed. Although DOJ was unable to supply all information listed in 36 CFR §1230.14

entities.name: Department of Justice Office of Inspector General

uncertainty_notes: Uncertainty exists over whether materials in the basement were the recordkeeping copy of federal records.
DOJ is unable to determine which records were lost in the flood versus electronic records maintained elsewhere.
It is unclear if personal device messages were later incorporated into a government recordkeeping system.
NARA considers the matter closed despite incomplete information regarding applicable records schedules and volume.

case.summary: NARA letter to DOJ EOUSA regarding an allegation that the interim U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia used Signal's disappearing messages feature to delete communications with a journalist.

evidence.statement: The allegation claims that the interim United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia may have used the disappearing message feature on the Signal messaging platform, which deleted electronic communications with a journalist.
evidence.quote: The allegation claims that the interim United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia may have used the disappearing message feature on the Signal messaging platform, which deleted electronic communications with a journalist.

evidence.statement: NARA requests that EOUSA investigate this allegation and respond within 30 calendar days.
evidence.quote: In accordance with 36 CFR 1230.14(a), NARA requests that EOUSA investigate this allegation and respond within 30 calendar days of the date of this letter.

evidence.statement: NARA requests a complete description of records, volume, dates, and disposition authority number if known.
evidence.quote: A complete description of the records with volume, dates, and applicable disposition authority number if known;

evidence.statement: NARA requests a statement of the exact circumstances surrounding the removal or destruction of records.
evidence.quote: A statement of the exact circumstances surrounding the removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records;

evidence.statement: NARA requests details of actions taken to salvage, retrieve, or reconstruct the records.
evidence.quote: Details of the actions taken to salvage, retrieve, or reconstruct the records.

evidence.statement: NARA requests EOUSA instruct staff that electronic messages are federal records regardless of platform.
evidence.quote: Additionally, please ensure that EOUSA clearly instructs all staff that electronic messages created in the course of or related to agency business are considered federal records and must be captured and managed according to a NARA-approved records schedule,

entities.name: Executive Office for United States Attorneys
interim United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia
Laurence Brewer
entities.role: Director, Office of Records Management Policy, DOJ

uncertainty_notes: The allegation states the interim U.S. Attorney 'may have used' Signal's disappearing messages; no finding of fact is made in this letter.
The letter requests information but does not confirm that unauthorized disposition occurred.
The specific journalist involved is not named in the provided text.
